# World Futures Day 2025: UNESCO advances futures literacy

This year's World Futures Day event on the theme “Anticipation in an Era of Volatility,” was organized on 2 December at UNESCO's Headquarters in Paris. The event brought together participants from around the globe to explore how futures literacy and foresight can enhance our anticipatory capacity to navigate global challenges in an era of technological transformation, climate change, demographic shifts and geopolitical instability.

9 December 2025 Last update: 24 February 2026

The public lecture was delivered by Éric Sadin, whose intervention, “The Future of Humanity in an Era of Omniscient Artificial Intelligence,” offered a provocative framing for the day. In a powerful critique of unbridled technological acceleration related to the rise of generative Artificial Intelligence. 

Human beings now have at their disposal tools that make the use of some of their essential attributes almost obsolete.

Éric Sadin

Speakers stressed the urgency of strengthening collective foresight and anticipation capabilities. The Assistant Director-General for Natural Sciences, and ad interim for Social and Human Sciences, Lidia Brito, reiterated the importance of long-term institutional readiness, noting “the need to guarantee that national governments have the capacity to really use and integrate anticipatory governance in their planning and to enhance crisis preparedness, and the role of research in identifying trends and risks”. 

On behalf of the Assistant Director-General for Education, Sobhi Tawil, Director of the Futures of Learning and Innovation Division, underlined that “the future of international cooperation in education will be shaped by our ability to anticipate change”. UNESCO should assume its dual role as laboratory of ideas and global leader in education, leveraging its global network of university-based UNESCO Chairs and centres of excellence. 

The Assistant Director-General for Communication and Information, Tawfik Jelassi, emphasized the importance of trust in information noting that “we want users of digital platforms to become media and information literate citizens. This is why more than 35 countries have already integrated UNESCO’s media and information literacy curriculum into their education systems.” 

We must not leave space for a technological race, for hegemony, monopoly and manipulation.

Mohamed Elfarnawany representing the Assistant Director-General for Priority Africa and External Relations

Speakers from different regions of the world also highlighted the need to shift from reactive governance to proactive, future-oriented decision-making. 

In Parliament, anticipation is about helping legislators move from crisis to future-shaping, […] so the decisions we take today don’t take away from the benefits of future generations.

Brenda Ogembo Deputy Head of the Senate Liaison Office at the Parliament of Kenya

As noted by Gustavo Merino, Director of Social Policies, in his concluding remarks “Anticipatory governance is indispensable for helping us to see beyond the noise of the present and make sense of social transformations. It is at the core of UNESCO’s Management of Social Transformations Programme.” 

Main outcomes included:

- Strategic insights for the development of UNESCO's Global Anticipatory Policy Coalition, led by UNESCO's Management of Social Transformations Programme, a new global platform aimed at fostering knowledge sharing, peer learning and capacity-building among governments and foresight experts to mainstream foresight and anticipatory policymaking worldwide - to be launched in June 2026.
- Recognition of the value of the international network of 1,100+ university-based UNESCO Chairs, including the 35 UNESCO Chairs in Futures Studies, as strategic “antennas” to detect and analyse emerging issues across different fields, regions and disciplines, thereby strengthening UNESCO's global futures literacy and foresight capacity. 
- Concrete demonstration, through panels and workshops, of how futures literacy and foresight can be practically applied on the futures of science, ethics of emerging technologies, proactive crises response and imagining Africa's futures - with contributions from all of UNESCO's Programme Sectors and UNESCO Chairs on futures literacy and foresight.
